clue.text: Hate-mail from 26 opponents in disorder on Right

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the jumble comes before the last letter
things in disorder are jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, a word for the best people
taken as written, as part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Someone receives abusive post sent by a chaotic band of political opponents on the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disorder' shuffles the 26-across answer together with OPPONENTS; 'on' sets R (Right) beneath them in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonymous malicious letter is the classic form of hate-mail, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sailor to expire whilst receiving whip, or give up

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to expire is to die
a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: A sailor facing death while being flogged might as well surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' is the containment signal; 'or' simply links wordplay to definition. The whip is the cat-o'-nine-tails, once used for naval floggings.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or responsibility, i.e. to relinquish it.

clue.text: Mike across the pond in deficit

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
across the pond, from Britain, means in America: IN US

explanation.surface: An American called Mike has gone into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' is British slang for the United States, so it gives IN US.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance that is negative is below zero, so an account in deficit is in the red.

clue.text: Cite this new moral philosopher

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a remade one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to quote a fresh thinker on ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of CITE THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in ethics studies right and wrong conduct, which is moral philosophy.

clue.text: Angel cuts up hearts

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: pares means trims or cuts
H is the abbreviation for the suit of hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A heavenly being slices hearts open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works only because this is a down light: the verb is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The seraphim are the highest order of angels in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Nature reserve and sacred place

definitions.meaning: a protected area for wildlife, e.g. a bird refuge
a holy area such as the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: A list of two kinds of protected ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a wildlife refuge and the holiest part of a temple or church.

clue.text: Move to secure king's confession

indicators.note: securing something means holding it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to shift is to move
R, from Latin rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: An attempt to obtain a monarch's admission of guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts R (king) inside SHIFT (move).
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is an old word for confession to a priest, as in short shrift before execution.

clue.text: Hamlet's name used in dreadful performance with kid

indicators.note: used in means placed within, so this letter goes inside the rest
a dreadful version is a wrecked one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the jumbled letters
taken as written, as part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's hero is named in an awful show starring a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' is the anagram signal for the two words after it, and 'used in' sets the abbreviation for name among the jumbled letters. 'Hamlet's' reads as possessive but is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is titled The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark: his royal title.

clue.text: In dungeon, but Eliot produced key!

indicators.note: produced here means made into something new, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys, A to G

explanation.surface: Imprisoned, the poet Eliot nonetheless came up with the means of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges BUT ELIOT, then E (a musical key) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon entered through a trapdoor, where prisoners were forgotten.

clue.text: Can't stand soldiers on violence charge

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge for assault
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops who are facing an assault charge find it intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: Actual bodily harm is a British assault charge; 'on' in an across clue puts the soldiers after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to find it unbearable, which is what being unable to stand it means.

clue.text: Small man — university student one pushes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
Tim is a man's name
L, for learner, stands for a student
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A short undergraduate gives someone a shove.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, as on British L-plates for new drivers, so it stands for student.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are prompts or incentives, the plural noun matching pushes in the sense of urgings.

clue.text: Something done about uranium sale

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: an action is a thing done
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Something has been done concerning a uranium deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps ACTION (something done) round U (uranium).
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Tide's sleep that engulfs Endymion at the start

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing whole, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: at the start means only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Endymion, the shepherd of myth, is engulfed in eternal sleep by the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes E from Endymion; 'that engulfs' puts it inside NAP (sleep).
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is the tide with the smallest range, occurring at the moon's quarters.

clue.text: Shadowy figure wrecking hotel suite

indicators.note: wrecking the words smashes their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark figure is seen trashing a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecking' rearranges HOTEL SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark outline shape seen against light, a shadow-like figure.

clue.text: Grass surrounding artists at pub is put down afresh

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the first piece wraps the rest

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: at means beside, so the artists sit next to the pub

parts.note: PH, public house, is a pub on British maps
RAs are Royal Academicians, i.e. artists

explanation.surface: Lawn round painters drinking at the pub gets newly laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the grass round the rest; 'at' joins the pub abbreviation to the Royal Academicians. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rephrase is to express in different words, i.e. to write something down again in new form.

clue.text: Group in most natural surroundings

definitions.meaning: a section or faction within a larger body
the setting where one is most at home

explanation.surface: A band of people feels most at home in familiar territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a faction within a body and the setting one is best suited to.

clue.text: Amusing person provided female's capital

parts.note: a card is a joker or witty character
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A funny person supplied a woman's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like funds but is the city: the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Leaves papers and note for false lover

parts.note: cress is a plant grown for its small edible leaves
ID, identity documents, are papers
A is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Salad leaves, documents and a love letter are left for an unfaithful partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida, in Troilus and Cressida, deserts Troilus for Diomedes: literature's model of an unfaithful woman.

clue.text: I must attend appointment with pigeon in swamp

parts.note: the nun is a breed of fancy pigeon with a hood-like crest
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Someone must keep a meeting with a bird in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must attend' and 'with' join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or overwhelm, just as to swamp is.

clue.text: Light-fitting for tenant?

parts.note: to light on something is to come down on it, i.e. to land
a holder is a fitting that grips something, like a lamp socket

explanation.surface: Asking for a lamp socket on behalf of an occupant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-fitting' reads as a lamp fitting, but light is the verb meaning alight or come down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant occupies property on lease, so is one who holds land; the question mark flags the loose example.

clue.text: One naughty little sister displaying cognition

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the word's letters are disordered

parts.note: sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: A mischievous younger sibling shows signs of understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles only the word 'One'; 'little sister' is shortened, not scrambled. 'displaying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Noesis is the philosophical term for intellectual apprehension: pure thinking or knowing.

clue.text: Say Marvin eats sweet vegetable

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Lee Marvin was a Hollywood actor, so Lee is one Marvin
a gum is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: An actor named Marvin munches a sugary vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Marvin as an example of a name: the Hollywood actor Lee Marvin. 'eats' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume is a pod plant such as a pea or bean eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Spinning bait in lake and river in Yorkshire

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An angler casts rotating bait in Yorkshire's lakes and rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: In spinning, a type of fishing, the bait is an artificial lure drawn through the water.

clue.text: Indispensable as in pen that's disposable

indicators.note: in means placed within, so these letters go inside the pen

parts.note: Bic is the famous brand of disposable ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A paradox: a cheap throwaway pen is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; the throwaway pen is the well-known brand, and 'as' is used just as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is fundamental and essential, so it cannot be done without.

clue.text: Bêche-de-mer good after time on vessel

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A sea cucumber is good after spending time on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a link here but the old word for 'concerning'. 'after' sends the good letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bêche-de-mer is the French name for the sea cucumber, also called trepang, eaten in Asian cooking.

clue.text: Mad sort out high status

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy type works their way to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MAD SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the condition of being a celebrity, a lofty public standing.

clue.text: Best drunk enters Spain twice

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
twice means the letter is used two times

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk crosses the Spanish border twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles E (Spain) and 'enters' puts LIT (drunk) between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choicest members of a group, the cream or the pick.

clue.text: I'd successfully woo model in sea abroad when it's chilly

indicators.note: in means placed within, so these pieces go inside the sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea
the apostrophe is ignored, giving ID
to win someone is to court them successfully
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T is a model

explanation.surface: A holiday romancer boasts of winning a model's heart by a foreign sea in the cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' asks for the French word for sea; 'in' places the rest inside it. Ford's Model T supplies the letter for model.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of winter is the coldest part of the year.
